responsibilities.name: Weekly TODO Sweep
responsibilities.instruction: Review the codebase for open TODOs, stale branches, and incomplete work items. Produce a structured report of what needs attention, what can be closed, and what should be prioritized next week.

context.purpose: Codebases accumulate TODOs, stale feature branches, and half-finished work throughout the week. Without periodic review, these pile up and create confusion about what is actually in progress vs. abandoned. This weekly sweep keeps the workspace clean and ensures nothing falls through the cracks.
process: STEP 1 — SCAN TODOs: Search the codebase for TODO, FIXME, HACK, and XXX comments. Collect file paths, line numbers, and the comment text. Run: `grep -rn 'TODO\|FIXME\|HACK\|XXX' --include='*.py' --include='*.ts' --include='*.js' --include='*.go' . | head -50`

STEP 2 — SCAN STALE BRANCHES: List all remote branches and their last commit date. Identify branches with no commits in the past 14 days. Run: `git branch -r --sort=-committerdate --format='%(committerdate:short) %(refname:short)' | head -30`
STEP 3 — CHECK OPEN WORK: Review MEMORY.md for any open items, pending tasks, or follow-ups that have not been addressed.
STEP 4 — TRIAGE: Classify each finding as: (a) ACTIVE — still in progress, keep, (b) STALE — no recent activity, candidate for cleanup, (c) DONE — completed but not cleaned up, should be removed.

STEP 5 — PRODUCE REPORT: Write a structured summary covering: count of TODOs by category, stale branches with recommended action (delete or revive), open work items with status, and top 3 priorities for next week.
context.success_criteria: A clear report is produced listing all open TODOs, stale branches, and incomplete work items with triage classifications. Stale branches older than 30 days are flagged for deletion. The report includes a prioritized list of items needing attention next week.
context.prior_learnings: Focus on actionable findings — don't report every single TODO if there are hundreds. Group by file or feature area. Stale branch detection should use committer date, not author date. Some TODOs are intentional long-term markers (e.g., 'TODO: optimize when traffic exceeds 10k rps') — don't flag these as stale.

responsibilities.name: Daily CI/CD Health Check
responsibilities.instruction: Check CI/CD pipeline health, recent build failures, and test regressions. Report any failing builds, flaky tests, or pipeline issues that need attention.

context.purpose: CI/CD pipeline health is critical for engineering velocity. Broken builds block the entire team, flaky tests erode trust in the test suite, and unnoticed regressions compound over time. A daily health check catches these problems early before they become costly.
process: STEP 1 — CHECK RECENT BUILDS: Review the most recent CI/CD build results. Look for failed builds on main/master and on active feature branches. Run: `git log --oneline -10 main` to see recent commits and correlate with build status.

STEP 2 — IDENTIFY FAILURES: For any failed builds, read the build logs to identify root cause. Classify failures as: (a) CODE — a code change broke the build, (b) FLAKY — intermittent test failure not caused by code changes, (c) INFRA — CI infrastructure issue (timeout, resource exhaustion, dependency resolution).

STEP 3 — CHECK TEST HEALTH: Look for patterns of test failures. Run the test suite if accessible: `pytest -v 2>&1 | tail -40` or `npm test 2>&1 | tail -40`. Note any tests that are consistently skipped or disabled.
STEP 4 — CHECK DEPENDENCIES: Look for outdated or vulnerable dependencies if tooling is available. Run: `npm audit --production 2>/dev/null` or `pip audit 2>/dev/null` or equivalent.

STEP 5 — PRODUCE REPORT: Summarize pipeline health with: current build status (passing/failing), number of recent failures and their classification, any flaky tests identified, dependency health, and recommended actions.
context.success_criteria: A clear health report is produced covering: main branch build status, count and classification of recent failures, identified flaky tests, and dependency health. Any critical issues (broken main, security vulnerabilities) are escalated immediately rather than just reported.
context.prior_learnings: Not all projects have CI/CD configured — if there is no CI pipeline, focus on running the test suite locally and checking dependency health. Flaky tests are best identified by looking for tests that fail intermittently across multiple runs — a single failure may just be a real bug. Always check if a failure on main was already fixed by a subsequent commit before escalating.
